knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The national prohibition commenced on 1 July 2024, as stated by DEWR, Asbestos Safety and the SA Government.
The import ban on engineered stone benchtops, panels and slabs took effect on 1 January 2025, as stated by DEWR and Asbestos Safety.
Installed engineered stone does not have to be removed, but work that removes, repairs or modifies it is restricted.
The August 2025 Safe Work Australia guidance says notification is required when work involves processing engineered stone, and that the regulator does not need to approve the work before it starts.
WorkSafe Victoria states the ban does not apply to natural stone and gives granite as an example of a benchtop that is not prohibited.
The what installed stone means section says the practical point is that the work is the problem, not the stone sitting in the kitchen.

practicalCriteria: States the engineered stone prohibition dates and the removal position accurately
Declines engineered stone processing in writing with the referral route
Does not imply that the work is lawful for the business
passRule: Knowledge checks: 4 of 5 correct (80%). Practical sign-off is separate and is not granted by the knowledge check: an assessor must observe every critical practical criterion and record it.
evidenceRequired: Enquiry record with the decision and referral
Written decline or referral sent to the client
stopWorkCriteria: Any request to process engineered stone without a confirmed regulator-compliant route
Any removal, repair or modification of installed engineered stone by the business
